questions.question: Discuss the impact of the French Revolution on the development of sociological thought.
questions.solution_html:
• French Revolution Impact: Promoted liberty and equality, influencing
  • sociological thought on social change.
  • Answer Key – MG3DSCSOC202: Social Life – Forms and
  • Dynamics
  • 17a. Emergence of Sociology from Revolutions
  • The Enlightenment fostered rational inquiry; the French Revolution
  • challenged feudalism and hierarchy; the Industrial Revolution generated
  • new urban classes and social problems. Together they institutionalised
  • sociology as a science addressing order and change.
  • 17b. Berger’s “Professional Peeper” Metaphor
  • Berger’s metaphor captures the sociologist’s curiosity and moral
  • responsibility. The sociologist observes everyday life critically yet ethically
  • unveiling taken-for-granted norms without voyeurism. It balances
  • detachment with empathy.
  • 18a. Education, Digitalisation, and Youth Identity
  • Digital technology shapes self-presentation, community, and values. In
  • Kerala, access to education and online culture reconfigures class, language
  • and gender relations, creating hybrid youth identities and new social
  • networks.
  • 18b. Transformation of Matrilineal System in Kerala
  • Transition from taravad (matrilineal joint family) to nuclear units eroded
  • female property rights but promoted individual autonomy. Legal reforms
  • (Marumakkathayam Act 1933) shifted inheritance and authority, redefining
  • gender dynamics.
  • 19a. Social Change and Indian National Movement
  • The movement fostered unity across caste and religion, promoted women’s
  • participation, and laid foundations of democratic citizenship. It embedded
  • nationalism within everyday moral life.
  • 19b. Tradition and Modernity in India
  • Indian modernity fuses continuity with change—ritual coexistence with
  • technology, caste persistence with new mobility. Sociological duality reveals
  • adaptation rather than rupture.
  • 20a. Functions of Mass Media
  • Media informs, educates, entertains, and socialises citizens, linking
  • individuals to the public sphere. It reinforces norms but also stimulates
  • reform through exposure and debate.
  • 20b. Glocalization in Culture
  • Global brands adapt to local tastes—McDonald’s India offers vegetarian
  • menus; fashion integrates traditional motifs with modern design. This
  • hybridization preserves cultural identity while embracing global influence.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
questions.final_answer: hybridization preserves cultural identity while embracing global influence.
